prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Hospital medication dispensing/returns. Aliases: Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Morrowglass validates/rejects/routes/statuses orders; produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Cinderwake reconciles orders/dispenses/balances using identifiers; preserves clinical/transaction evidence; verifies authorization, excludes cancellations/superseded orders, flags duplicates, calculates conservative remainders. Disagreements hold; corrections require authorized orders. Clinical Pharmacist produces Dose Exception Review Slip; escalates inconclusive exceptions. Juniper verifies order/product/strength/quantity, blocks discrepant/unauthorized releases, produces evidenced Batch Release Note. Cinderwake stops affected picks, secures stock/evidence, produces Priority Refill Tote Tag. Copperfield prepares/rechecks/reconciles replenishment, never decides doses; produces Cold Chain Handoff Card. Hospital Courier accepts suitable closed loads; produces Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record. Pneumatic Tube Network reconciles compliance/identifiers/destination. East Tube Dispatch Console sends Tube Route Exception Ticket; West Tube Dispatch Console authorizes routing. Operations coordinates alternatives; faults hold; restart requires checks/tests/authorization. Receiving staff verify/isolate; unresolved stocking prohibited. Charge Nurse sends Cabinet Downtime Notice. South Ward Cabinet Controller reports failures; both controllers record arrivals/block held/Out of Service dispensing until Ready for Dispense. North Ward Cabinet Controller uses tote tag; approved versioned configuration defines locations/product-identities/thresholds/roles/limits, effective time/approver. Availability=confirmed inventory plus recorded movements; replenishment limits cannot override clinical restrictions. Authenticate appropriate roles; high-risk removals may require confirmation; reject identity-mapping mismatches; missing current configuration blocks routine dispensing/reports investigation. Bluejay logs compartment temperatures/limits, probe/calibration/intervals, lot/expiry, authorized-access identities/times/stock and door duration. Excursion/probe-unavailability blocks stock; preserve environment. Compare handoff custody/history. Clinical Pharmacist decides release/quarantine/discard; retain lot disposition/block ineligible selection. Offline alarms persist; records retained until reconnection. Larkspur locks transactions/confirms nonadministration/escalates; no bypass/substitution. Tallowmere reconciles/segregates/secures returns; produces Return Bin Audit

New part:
S183: East Tube Dispatch Console maintains the approved route map and the current availability status of supported pneumatic segments.
S184: East Tube Dispatch Console checks the selected route against the destination cabinet, current network availability, and approved routing configuration before releasing a capsule.
S185: The console confirms that the destination is reachable and that the route does not include a segment reported unavailable.
S186: Route selection uses the destination identifier and the latest approved configuration version rather than an operator-entered sequence of segments.
S187: Before dispatch, the console checks for conflicting capsule movements and confirms that required interlocks are satisfied.
S188: The Pneumatic Tube Network reports segment status, transfer progress, and delivery confirmation to the dispatch console.
S189: If route status is stale or incomplete, the console holds the capsule and displays the condition for operator review.
S190: A loss of communication with a route sensor prevents the console from treating the affected segment as available.
S191: An interruption during transit is recorded with the capsule identifier, last confirmed location, and time of the interruption.
S192: The console alerts a Pharmacy Technician when a transfer stops progressing or cannot be confirmed at its destination.
S193: After recovery, the console requires refreshed segment status and an approved route decision before dispatch resumes.
S194: Route and temperature records retain timestamps and equipment identifiers to support operational review and investigation.
S195: The Pharmacy Verification Station serves as the final controlled checkpoint before a medication is made available for dispensing.
S196: The Clinical Pharmacist compares the active medication order with the product, strength, dosage form, dose, route, and scheduled time.
S197: The Clinical Pharmacist also confirms that the patient identifiers and pharmacy label agree with the authorized order.
S198: The Pharmacy Technician checks package integrity, lot identification, and expiry before presenting the medication for verification.
S199: For designated high-risk medications, an independent second check is completed and recorded before authorization.
S200: Any mismatch places the medication on hold until the discrepancy is resolved by an authorized pharmacy professional.
S201: The verification record captures the approving staff identity, time, and medication identifiers for later review.
S202: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot remains inhibited from completing a dispense until the required pharmacy authorization is present.
S203: The Clinical Pharmacist resolves unclear or conflicting order details through the Medication Order Gateway before authorizing release.
S204: The South Ward Cabinet Controller receives the release note and applies its own approved cabinet configuration before enabling any compartment.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
